completion_data.completion_summary: Closed task 144's final phase: re-verified the operator's completed token-provisioning and system-switch work live, substituted a non-sudo convergence proof for the one criterion that still needed sudo, and recorded exactly two reasoned exclusions (the interactive bootstrap run; the literal second sudo switch) rather than claiming unearned completion.

sapience_notes.note: A sudo-gated 'second switch is a no-op' convergence proof has a non-sudo substitute: compare `readlink -f /run/current-system` against a non-activating `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.<host>.config.system.build.toplevel --no-link --print-out-paths`. Identical store paths prove the flake's current evaluation already matches the live system exactly, which is a stronger and more direct proof than diffing a second switch's stdout output would have given, and requires no elevated privilege at all.

sops-install-secrets populating /run/secrets/<name> at the declared owner/mode is itself sufficient evidence that a full `sudo nixos-rebuild switch` (not merely a build) actually ran and activated -- the secret only materializes at system activation time, so its presence plus correct owner/mode is a reliable, independently-checkable proxy for 'the system switch completed', usable even when the agent cannot run sudo itself to confirm it directly.

Decision: when an operator-gated plan phase's blocking condition is subsequently resolved by the operator (here: real token added via sops, sudo nixos-rebuild switch run), the correct close is to re-verify the live evidence independently rather than trust the relayed report, then apply the plan's own original Closure rule (COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS with a Reasoned Exclusions table) rather than leave a prior dispatch-level BLOCKED override in place past the point its own stated obstruction was resolved.

users.users.<name>.linger declared at the NixOS layer plus a successful system switch is independently verifiable post-hoc via `loginctl show-user <name> --property=Linger` reporting Linger=yes, with no need to have observed the switch itself run -- the property is a durable system-activation side effect, not a transient log line.
